dossier.headline: The rupee has swung from a two-month low to a sharp recovery, with the RBI visible throughout
dossier.summary: The rupee weakened to a two-month low of 96.16 per dollar in late September and stayed under pressure whenever oil was elevated. It recovered through late October and into November, and one report has it closing at 93.91 on Friday, up 56 paise, helped by inflows and lower crude. The RBI is reported to have been active on both sides, buying dollars near 93.88 to cap the gains.
why_it_matters: A weaker rupee raises the cost of imported crude and feeds inflation, which the notes link back to RBI policy.
Currency direction affects the value of foreign inflows and the earnings of IT exporters.
Visible RBI intervention caps moves in both directions.

moved.name: IT exporters
moved.line: Benefit from a weaker rupee; the relationship is noted through the period.

watch: Whether the RBI keeps absorbing dollars near 93.88 and caps further gains.
Crude, which the notes tie directly to rupee direction.
Whether the recent foreign inflows persist.
questions: How much of the recovery is flows and how much is cheaper oil?
Is the RBI defending a level or just smoothing the move?
conflicts: Reports differ on Wednesday's close, 95.22 against 95.28 (note of 2026-10-29 1100).
Friday's 93.91 close is attributed to one report only (note of 2026-11-07 0800).
